# omekasr

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-universe version](https://giocomai.r-universe.dev/omekasr/badges/version)](https://giocomai.r-universe.dev/omekasr)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of `omekasr` is to facilitate interaction with the Omeka S REST API. 

It is currently only minimally functional. Features are documented in this document as they are introduced and tested.

Planned features include:

- producing pdf reports of Omeka S items

## Installation

You can install the development version of `omekasr` from its main repository on Codeberg:

``` r
remotes::install_git("https://codeberg.org/giocomai/omekasr")
```

or from r-universe with:

``` r
install.packages("omekasr", repos = c("https://giocomai.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```

## Introducing `omekasr`

The first thing you do when working with `omekasr` is to set the url of the Omeka S instance you want to work with. Throughout the documentation, a dedicated testing instance will be used for reference; its contents are derived from the [Omeka S official sandbox instance](https://dev.omeka.org/omeka-s-sandbox/).

Using `o_set()` will set the base url for the current session.

```{r o_set}
library("omekasr")
o_set(base_url = "https://omekasr.giorgiocomai.eu/")
```

Internally, this will check that the given input appears to be a valid URL, and will append `api` as requested by Omeka S. This test can be conducted interactively with `o_check_url()`.


```{r o_check_url}
o_check_url()
```

This only checks that the URL appears to be valid, but does not ensure that an active Omeka S server is responeding at that address.


## Retrieve items and properties

It is possible to retrieve an data from any supported endpoint with `o_get()`; at present, only `items` and `properties` are supported

```{r o_get}
get_response <- o_get(id = 12, type = "items")

```

Main types have also convenience functions that return an `S7` object that actively identifies the response as an Omeka S item.


```{r o_get_item}
item <- o_get_item(item_id = 12)

item
```


```{r item class}
class(item)
```

## Troubleshooting

This package features a situation report function, that can be used to troubleshoot most common issues, such as incorrect API base url or lack of internet connection

```{r o_sitrep}
o_sitrep()
```
